title: Ancient Stalagmite Reveals Monsoon History in Meghalaya
description: A recent study of a stalagmite from Mawsmai Cave in Meghalaya has unveiled significant insights into the historical patterns of monsoon in northeastern India. Researchers reconstructed a 6,000-year climate record, revealing fluctuations in rainfall intensity influenced by global climate systems and solar activity. The findings highlight the importance of understanding long-term monsoon variability, crucial for agriculture and water supply in South Asia. This research not only sheds light on ancient climate conditions but also emphasizes the interconnectedness of regional and global climate processes.

title: India to oppose EU carbon tax and fossil fuel phase-out at COP31
description: India is set to challenge unilateral trade barriers and resist global pressures to phase out fossil fuels, prioritising its domestic industrial interests and developmental energy requirements. Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav detailed this stance on Tuesday, ahead of the UN climate conference (COP31) scheduled for November 9-20 in Antalya, Turkiye. A primary point of contention is the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which became operational on January 1. By imposing a border tax on carbon-intensive imports-specifically iron, steel, aluminium, and cement-the EU is effectively increasing the cost of entry for Indian exports into the 27-nation bloc. India views this as a discriminatory and protectionist measure that unfairly penalises businesses in developing economies for embedded emissions. This position is not isolated; during the September BRICS summit under India's chairship, member nations including China, Russia, Brazil, and South Africa collectively condemned such unilateral trade barriers as punitive and discriminatory.

title: China seeks to bring archaeology closer to public
description: BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- China is seeking to bring archaeology closer to the public, with a new five-year plan setting out priorities for research, international cooperation and the wider presentation of archaeological findings. China now has 65 national archaeological site parks, which are increasingly becoming visitor destinations. Visits to these parks rose from 20.97 million in 2021 to 97.74 million in 202
